title: Runtime padding shepherding & length-aware coalescer to reduce wasted tokens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: implement a lightweight "shepherding" layer and a length-aware coalescer that reduces padding-induced waste across prefill+decode paths and pairs sequence-length buckets with kernel profiles. The feature should: (1) opportunistically reorder prefill work within a short time window to coalesce similar sequence-length requests, (2) enforce a soft padding budget per micro-batch to allow small truncation or prefix coalescing when tail padding exceeds threshold, and (3) annotate buckets with kernel affinity so the runtime avoids repeated kernel rebinds during a scheduling epoch. Expected outcome: 10–35% reduction in total token compute for typical chat workloads (observed in initial trace-driven simulation), improved GPU utilization, and fewer kernel selection thrash events that spike latency.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration tests demonstrating >=10% compute reduction on internal chat benchmark (mix of short/long requests)
No regression in 99th-percentile latency by more than 5% under nominal load
Graceful fallback when shepherding window expires (no request starvation)
Metricization: new dashboard panels showing padding savings, kernel-affinity collisions, and shepherding reorder rate
description_notes: Design notes: we introduce a "slot" abstraction for micro-batch assembly (10–50ms window) and maintain per-slot soft budgets: max_padding_ratio (default 0.35) and kernel-affinity-penalty. The coalescer will prefer grouping by effective_seq_len (prefill_len + estimated_decode_len) and then by kernel affinity. A small, best-effort prefix-coalescing step can merge short prefixes to reduce KV-cache duplication in prefill-heavy traffic. Implementation will be in two phases: (A) simulation & trace replay + perf harness, (B) guarded rollout behind feature-flag with telemetry. Tradeoffs: slight added scheduling jitter (configurable) vs net compute savings; complexity added to scheduler which may affect maintainability; we will keep shepherding disabled for constrained-latency routes (route metadata flag).
